article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 55% Indica / 45% Sativa
Genetics: Purple Punch × Lemon Drizzle
Breeder: Barney’s Farm
THC Content: 28%
CBD Content: 0.3%
Terpene Profile: Limonene , beta-caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Blueberry, sweet grape, sour citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–65 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: First to second week of October
Indoor Yield: 550–650 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 1,500 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Purple Punch x Lemon Drizzle takes two very different approaches to flavor and forces them into the same flower. One side brings the dark sweetness of grapes, blueberries, and creamy dessert notes; the other delivers tart lemon rind, earth, and the brighter energy associated with Haze-influenced cannabis . The combination produces marijuana that can smell like blueberry pie finished with fresh citrus zest rather than another straightforward grape strain .

Barney’s Farm developed this slightly indica-dominant hybrid by crossing Purple Punch with Lemon Drizzle, creating a plant that retains the dense flowers and physical calm of its purple parent while gaining greater mental lift and aromatic sharpness from its lemon-heavy counterpart. With THC reaching about 28%, substantial resin production, and indoor yields approaching 650 g/m², the cultivar balances boutique flower quality with practical growing characteristics.
Genetics and Lineage

Purple Punch contributes the heavier and sweeter half of the pedigree. Its lineage comes from Larry OG crossed with Granddaddy Purple , joining two important branches of California cannabis. Granddaddy Purple adds the familiar grape, berry, and dark-fruit profile along with compact growth and the ability to develop dramatic violet coloration. Larry OG reinforces the Kush side with citrus, pine, earth, resin production, and pronounced physical relaxation. Together, those genetics give Purple Punch its dense flowers, dessert-like aroma, and deeply relaxing finish.

Lemon Drizzle moves the cross in almost the opposite direction. Barney’s Farm developed that cultivar from Super Lemon Haze and OG Kush , creating an 85% sativa parent with vigorous growth and a pronounced citrus profile. Super Lemon Haze itself combines Super Silver Haze with Lemon Skunk , contributing bright lemon, incense, spice, and energetic cerebral qualities. OG Kush adds enough density, earthiness, and resin to prevent Lemon Drizzle from becoming an excessively loose or lanky Haze expression.

Combining these parents results in a 55% indica and 45% sativa hybrid whose genetic balance is unusually close. Purple Punch supplies grape sweetness, color, density, and body relaxation, while Lemon Drizzle contributes sour citrus, additional vigor, and a more animated mental character. That division explains why the finished strain can feel more energetic than its Purple Punch ancestry suggests without losing the heavier relaxation expected from an indica-leaning cultivar.
Effects and Experience

The experience usually begins above the shoulders. A noticeable mood lift can arrive fairly quickly, bringing increased interest in conversation, music, movies, gaming, or creative activities. The Lemon Drizzle side gives the early phase a clearer and more upbeat character than conventional Purple Punch, and moderate doses may preserve enough motivation for low-pressure activities. It is not a sharp, racing Haze effect, but there is enough cerebral movement to keep the high from feeling immediately sleepy.

Physical relaxation becomes more obvious as the session progresses. Tightness can ease through the shoulders and limbs while the mental energy gradually becomes smoother and less demanding. This middle stage is where the genetic balance works particularly well: the user may feel distinctly high and physically comfortable without necessarily becoming immobilized. Larger amounts shift that balance toward the Purple Punch side, increasing body weight and reducing the desire to remain active.

At approximately 28% THC, this marijuana strain belongs firmly in the high-potency category. Inexperienced consumers should approach it conservatively because an excessive dose can produce dizziness, dry mouth, dry eyes, racing thoughts, or temporary anxiety. Smaller servings are more likely to preserve the enjoyable contrast between uplifting cerebral effects and gradual body relaxation rather than pushing the experience directly toward sedation.
Medical Benefits

The mixed cerebral and physical profile may appeal to medical cannabis consumers looking for something more flexible than a purely sedating indica. Stress and difficulty mentally disengaging are common reasons people gravitate toward hybrids of this type. The brighter early phase can shift attention away from repetitive thoughts, while the later physical calm may help the body settle as the experience develops.

Persistent discomfort and muscular tension are other areas where the heavier portion of the high may be relevant. THC can influence pain perception through the endocannabinoid system and related neurological pathways, and the strain’s increasingly relaxed physical character may make aches feel less intrusive. Larger evening doses may also become sleepy for some consumers, although the Lemon Drizzle ancestry can make the first part of the experience too mentally active for people seeking immediate sedation.

The strain contains little CBD, so its effects are primarily driven by THC and aromatic compounds rather than a balanced THC-to-CBD ratio. Limonene helps shape the sharp citrus profile, while beta-caryophyllene contributes spice and can interact with CB2 receptors. Myrcene adds earthy and herbal depth. Individual responses to whole-flower cannabis remain highly variable, making actual cannabinoid testing and careful dosing more useful than relying on a strain name alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

A well-cured flower can smell like two different cannabis families layered together. Blueberry and sweet grape provide the darker fruit foundation, often creating an impression reminiscent of berry pie or grape candy. Sour lemon quickly cuts through that sweetness, giving the aroma a sharper edge. Creamy vanilla appears underneath the fruit, while earth and light Kush-like pungency prevent the bouquet from becoming overly sugary.

Limonene is an obvious contributor to the lemon and citrus-peel qualities. Caryophyllene can add pepper and dry spice, while myrcene supplies earth, herbs, and some of the deeper fruit character. Purple Punch-leaning phenotypes may emphasize berries, grape, and creamy sweetness, whereas plants expressing more Lemon Drizzle can produce sharper citrus, pine, and faintly Haze-like herbal notes.

The flavor generally opens with sweet berry and grape before tart citrus becomes more prominent through the middle of the inhale. Creamy vanilla can soften the transition, while earth and spice remain on the exhale. Vaporization at moderate temperatures tends to reveal the berry and lemon contrast particularly well. A rushed dry can erase much of that detail, making controlled curing important for preserving the cultivar’s most distinctive feature: the meeting of dark dessert fruit and bright sour citrus.
Growing Information

Purple Punch x Lemon Drizzle grows with more vigor than a typical compact Purple Punch while remaining considerably easier to control than a strongly Haze-dominant plant. Indoor specimens generally finish around 100–120 centimeters. Outdoors, mature plants can reach approximately 150–180 centimeters when provided with sufficient root space and a full season. The structure provides enough side branching for canopy training without creating an excessive amount of stretch.

Topping during healthy vegetative growth can produce several strong leaders, and low-stress training helps spread those branches across the available light footprint. A Screen of Green setup also works well because the cultivar can fill horizontal space efficiently. Removing weak lower branches before flowering directs resources toward productive tops and improves airflow through the center of the canopy.

Indoor flowering takes approximately 60–65 days. Flowers typically develop into dense, resinous clusters, and Purple Punch genetics may produce increasingly dark coloration as maturity approaches. Cooler nighttime temperatures can enhance purple expression in genetically predisposed plants, although intentionally subjecting cannabis to severe cold is unnecessary and can reduce growth. The flowers themselves can become heavy, so branches may benefit from trellis netting or stakes during the final weeks.

Indoor yield potential is approximately 550–650 grams per square meter in a well-managed environment. Achieving the upper range requires adequate light intensity, healthy roots, even canopy development, stable irrigation, and appropriate temperature and humidity. The strain does not require extreme feeding to perform well; gradual nutrition based on plant demand is generally more useful than pushing fertilizer concentration simply to chase yield.

Outdoors, the hybrid can produce around 1,500 grams per plant under exceptional conditions. That figure should be considered genetic potential rather than an average harvest. Large production requires abundant sunlight, generous soil or container volume, early establishment, consistent irrigation, good nutrition, and favorable weather throughout the season.

Harvest normally falls during the first or second week of October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates. Because the flowers can become dense, growers in regions with rainy autumns should pay close attention to airflow and weather forecasts near maturity. Opening crowded interior growth and keeping branches separated can help prevent moisture from remaining trapped among thick buds.

Resin production is another strong cultivation trait inherited from both sides of the pedigree. Purple Punch and OG-influenced genetics contribute substantial trichome coverage, while Lemon Drizzle adds aromatic intensity. Properly selected material can therefore work well for dry sift, ice-water hash, or rosin in addition to dried flower.
FAQ
What strains make Purple Punch x Lemon Drizzle?

Barney’s Farm created the strain by crossing Purple Punch with Lemon Drizzle. Purple Punch descends from Larry OG and Granddaddy Purple, while Lemon Drizzle combines Super Lemon Haze with OG Kush. The complete pedigree therefore connects Granddaddy Purple, OG-family genetics, Super Lemon Haze, and Lemon Skunk-related ancestry.
Is Purple Punch x Lemon Drizzle indica or sativa?

It is approximately 55% indica and 45% sativa, making it a nearly balanced hybrid with a slight indica lean. The cerebral effects often appear first, while greater physical relaxation develops later. Its plant structure also reflects the balance, combining manageable indoor height with relatively vigorous lateral growth.
How much THC is in Purple Punch x Lemon Drizzle?

Current Barney’s Farm specifications place THC at approximately 28%. Earlier breeder catalog material listed approximately 24–26%, so actual batches can vary according to phenotype, cultivation, harvest timing, curing, storage, and laboratory methodology. Regardless of the exact test result, it should be considered a potent strain.
What does Purple Punch x Lemon Drizzle taste like?

The primary flavors include blueberry, sweet grape, sour citrus, creamy vanilla, and earth. Purple Punch supplies the darker berry and dessert characteristics, while Lemon Drizzle introduces tart lemon and brighter citrus. The resulting contrast is sweeter and more complex than a conventional lemon strain and sharper than typical Purple Punch.
How long does Purple Punch x Lemon Drizzle take to flower?

Indoor flowering generally takes approximately 60–65 days. Outdoors, the cultivar usually finishes during the first or second week of October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates. Final harvest timing should still be based on trichome maturity, flower development, plant health, and local weather conditions.
Final Thoughts on Purple Punch x Lemon Drizzle

Purple Punch x Lemon Drizzle succeeds because its parents contribute qualities that would normally seem to pull cannabis in opposite directions. Purple Punch brings dense flowers, grape and blueberry sweetness, purple coloration, and heavy Kush-influenced relaxation. Lemon Drizzle answers with sharp citrus, additional vigor, Haze-derived mental energy, and a more animated early experience.

The flavor captures that contrast especially well. Sweet grape and berry move into sour lemon before creamy vanilla, earth, and light spice complete the profile. Its effects follow a similar arc, starting euphoric and uplifting before gradually settling into a calmer physical state. With THC around 28%, careful dosing allows those stages to remain distinct rather than collapsing into an excessively heavy high.

Growers receive a practical combination of manageable height, 60–65 day flowering, strong resin development, and indoor yields approaching 650 g/m². Outdoor plants can become substantially larger and potentially produce around 1.5 kilograms each under ideal conditions before an early-October harvest.

For anyone interested in modern weed that combines purple dessert genetics with genuinely sharp citrus, Purple Punch x Lemon Drizzle offers more than a novelty cross. Its closely balanced indica-sativa makeup, layered flavor, substantial potency, and productive growth make it a distinctive hybrid whose two parent lines remain clearly recognizable in the finished flower.
